newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-EU aviation talks to begin Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-EU aviation talks to begin Wednesday.

text.p: The United States and the European Union will begin aviation talks Wednesday intended to set the stage for an "open skies" agreement between the two economic powerhouses, a European Commission aviation official said Tuesday.

"What we would like -- this is our main objective, our basic objective -- is to replace limited links between them by one ... free and fair aviation area," European Commission Air Transport Director Claude Chene told a briefing for reporters.

U.S. officials, however, made clear that the meeting with the Europeans, including representatives from 14 of the 15 European Union member-countries, were not actual negotiations but an exchange of information.
"They are discussions, not formal negotiations," a Transportation Department spokesman said of the talks, which are expected to continue through Thursday morning.

Chene said while airlines were behaving more and more like global entities, countries have lagged behind in eliminating controls over these carriers as they operate between various regions of the world.

"They are concluding alliances with other airlines and they are already almost integrated," he said, adding, "Unfortunately, the regulations, the organisations, the regime, has not followed the same line."
Even where the United States and European countries have concluded "open skies" agreements givng airlines freer rein, some loopholes and shortcomings exist, Chene said.
He said the talks would likely take many months, with the outcome still uncertain.

Chene explained that initial discussions would centre on issues of airline control and ownership, competition, settlement and dispute, computer reservations systems, commercial arrangements, leasing and safety.
In the event of progress in these areas, the Europeans would consider broader discussions covering all aspects of open skies over the Atlantic, including market access and traffic rights, Chene said.
